+  precondition_signals: ['stamp', 'sharedMount'],

The last unbuilt piece of #768's Phases 1–3, plus the guard that makes flipping a repo safe. You chose canary-first, and this is what has to land before any flip can mean anything.

**Still inert for every member**: each repo declares no mechanism, is served by baselining, and the new worker exits before it clones. Nothing changes until a declaration says otherwise.

## The skew guard moves into the engine

It was in `updates/`, which is canon-internal and never vendored — so baselining's worker, which runs from a member's own **mount**, could not have read it. A guard only half the system obeys is worse than none, so it now lives at `engine/served-by.mjs` and both sides read one definition.

**Baselining now stands down** for a repo the update flows serve, first thing, before any clone or write. Quiet and agentless: a repo served elsewhere is not an anomaly.

One lag worth naming: a member's worker is only as new as its last converge, so a repo flipped before its mount carries this check keeps baselining for one more cycle. That is the safe direction for the lag to point — it converges twice by the old mechanism rather than falling between the two. **Nothing can be served by both, and nothing by neither.**

## The runner

`packs/basics/tasks/update/` — a task in the same 02:00 slot, with the same two-stage shape as baselining. Its worker clones canon fresh and executes the *clone's* flows, never the mount's stale copies; delivers on a dated branch; and acts on `terminalFor`:

- **merge** → the shared landing helper, per the repo's delivery setting.
- **needs-human** → PR stays open, labelled, run stops.
- **apply-stage** → the agent stage is requested with its brief; nothing merges first.

**Engine before packs, always.** A pack declares the minimum engine it runs on and the pack flow enforces that against what the repo *has* — so running packs first would check every one against yesterday's engine and block updates the very next step would have made legal. And a refused engine update wins the terminal outright: nothing downstream of it is trustworthy, including a pack flow that never ran.

The I/O half is deliberately modelled line-for-line on baselining's rather than improved. That worker is the proven pattern; a cleverer second shape would be a second set of the same bugs.

## Tests

The git-free surface — branch naming, the PR text a human reads when a run stops, and **both halves of the stand-down**, each driven through the real `main()` against a real directory because the property that matters is that they stand down *before* the clone. Plus a drift guard across the seam: every terminal the runner branches on must be one the flows can actually produce.

The clone/push/PR half awaits the live pilot, as baselining's does.

## What has to happen before the canary is flipped

1. This merges.
2. The canary **converges once** so its mount carries the new engine and the new worker. **Its converge is currently broken** — it has been stamped 2026-08-05 for seven days ([Sheepdog#168](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/issues/168)) — so that is the real first step, and flipping before it would strand the repo with neither mechanism running a current worker.
3. Then write `maintenance.mechanism: "updates"` into its declaration and watch a full cycle.

**The flip cannot be first, though**, and the order matters:

1. **#783 merges.**
2. **The canary converges once**, so its mount carries the new engine and the new worker. A member's worker is only as new as its last converge, so a repo flipped before that keeps baselining for a cycle — safe, but it means the flip does nothing until the mount catches up.
3. **Then flip** `maintenance.mechanism: "updates"` and watch a full cycle.

Step 2 is the blocker: **ClaudiniteCanary has been stamped 2026-08-05 for seven days** ([Sheepdog#168](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/issues/168)). Its converge is failing silently, so it will not pick up the new worker on its own. Fixing that is now the critical path to the pilot — and it is worth fixing regardless, since a canary that has not converged in a week is not qualifying anything.

adding this task changes nothing for any member until someone writes that
flag: today every repo declares nothing, is served by baselining, and this
worker exits before it clones.

CI passed — 42 seconds for the unit tests, whole job green. The earlier "stuck" readings were a stale API view, not a slow run.

**[#783](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/783)** — the update runner, and the guard that makes flipping safe:

- **The skew guard moved into the engine.** It was in `updates/`, which is canon-internal and never vendored — so baselining's worker, running from a member's own *mount*, could never have read it. A guard only half the system obeys is worse than none.
- **Baselining now stands down** for a repo the update flows serve, before any clone or write. Both halves of that stand-down are tested through the real `main()` against a real directory, because the property that matters is the *ordering*.
- **The runner** (`packs/basics/tasks/update/`) clones canon fresh, runs the flows, delivers on a dated branch, and acts on the terminal: merge, leave-and-label, or hand off the apply stage. Engine before packs always — a pack's `minEngineVersion` is checked against what the repo *has*, so packs-first would block updates the next step would legalise.

One thing worth flagging: **CI didn't fire on this PR at all** — zero check runs — so I dispatched `ci.yml` explicitly, which is exactly what its `workflow_dispatch` trigger exists for. Worth knowing if it recurs.

**On the flip you asked for**, the order has to be: this merges → the canary converges once so its mount carries the new worker → then flip. Step two is blocked: ClaudiniteCanary has been stamped 2026-08-05 for seven days, so it won't pick up the new worker on its own. Flipping before that would leave it running an old worker that doesn't know about the flag. Fixing its converge is the real critical path to the pilot — and worth doing regardless, since a canary that hasn't converged in a week isn't qualifying anything.

Blocking the canary flip: [Sheepdog#168](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/issues/168) — the canary's broken converge.
